h1: At Pingnakorn Riverside — A Colonial Boutique on the Ping River with Rooms Bigger Than the Price
intro: Picture this: a pale colonial-style building with high roofs and timber balconies, sitting on a quiet stretch of the Ping River in Wat Ket — At Pingnakorn Riverside is a midrange boutique hotel that channels the architecture of King Rama V's era blended with applied Lanna design · The detail people talk about most is that standard rooms start at 42 sqm, far larger than hotels at the same price, alongside a riverside breakfast praised for its variety · 62 rooms, from approx. THB 1,400/night.

body.html: At Pingnakorn Riverside opened in 2016 and went through a major renovation in 2024 · The building was deliberately designed in an Eastern Colonial style blended with applied Lanna architecture from the reign of King Rama V, evoking the old trading days along the Ping River · Many reviews agree that walking into the lobby feels like stepping into a well-kept heritage hotel rather than a new build dressed up to look old.

There are 62 rooms in total, with standard Deluxe rooms starting at a generous 42 sqm — larger than many similarly priced rooms in Chiang Mai · Suites such as the Junior Suite and Family Suite stretch to 78–85 sqm, ideal for families · The roomy bathrooms get frequent praise · The decor leans on timber tones and vintage furnishings to match the concept throughout the property.
"The room was much bigger than expected and the bathroom was huge. The riverside setting is calm and quiet, and waking up to a buffet beside the Ping River felt like great value."

The highlight is the outdoor saltwater pool with a Jacuzzi and a children's pool in a leafy setting, plus the Nakara restaurant overlooking the Ping River · Breakfast is praised for its variety and good coffee, and several guests say it is the reason they happily got up early · The east-bank riverside setting is noticeably quieter than the city-centre side, ideal for travellers who want to escape the bustle while staying a short drive from the tourist areas.

The hotel sits on Charoen Rat Road in Wat Ket, on the east bank of the Ping River · It is about 10–15 minutes by car from the Night Bazaar and the Old City · Wat Ket itself has charm, with old temples, riverside cafés and Warorot Market (Kad Luang) a short ride away · The honest caveat is that walking into town takes over 30 minutes, so most reviews recommend relying on Grab or the hotel car.

The honest downsides are noise and the age of some rooms · Several reviews note that soundproofing between rooms and from the corridor is weak, so you may hear your neighbours · Some guests found beds hard or creaky, a few rooms have ageing furniture or mould in the bathroom, and breakfast is occasionally slow or not kept hot throughout · Wi-Fi is also unreliable in spots despite showing full signal.

The overall score sits at 9.2 from 178 reviews on Trip.com and 4.2/5 on TripAdvisor · Service scores especially high (friendly, attentive staff), followed by cleanliness and location · These numbers reflect a guest base that mostly leaves impressed by the spacious rooms, the riverside setting and the value, despite the gripes about noise and age-related details.

The verdict from real guest reviews: At Pingnakorn Riverside is best for travellers who want spacious rooms and a quiet riverside setting on a midrange budget and don't mind a short drive into town · The colonial design and the breakfast beside the Ping River make it feel like more than its price · If you are a light sleeper or want to walk straight into the tourist areas, this may not be it — ask for a recently renovated room away from the corridor first.

honestSummary: At Pingnakorn Riverside is the best pick for travellers who want spacious rooms, a quiet riverside setting and colonial design on a midrange budget — rooms from 42 sqm, an outdoor saltwater pool and breakfast beside the Ping River · You do have to accept weak soundproofing, a longish trip into town, and a few rooms that show their age.
honestChecks: If you are a light sleeper sensitive to noise — soundproofing between rooms and from the corridor is weak, so you may hear neighbours → ask for a room away from the corridor or on a quiet floor up front.

If you want to walk straight into the tourist areas — it takes over 30 minutes on foot into town, so you rely on Grab or the hotel car → budget for transport and time, or consider a city-centre stay if you have no car.

If you expect a flawless brand-new room throughout — the building opened in 2016 and, despite the 2024 renovation, some rooms still have hard beds or older furniture → request a recently renovated room and check its condition at check-in.

tips.title: Ask for a room away from the corridor
tips.body: Soundproofing is weak, so request a room not next to the corridor or on a quiet floor, and ask for a recently renovated one if you sleep lightly.

tips.title: Get up for the riverside buffet
tips.body: Breakfast is served beside the Ping River at Nakara with good coffee — go around the 7am opening for the freshest food and the best river-view seats.

tips.title: Plan your transport
tips.body: Town is too far to walk — have the front desk call a Grab or check the hotel car schedule, and allow extra time in high season when cars are scarce.

tips.title: Compare rates before high season
tips.body: November–February rates climb quickly — compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com and lock in a free-cancellation rate first.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — At Pingnakorn Riverside Chiang Mai

faq.q: Where is At Pingnakorn Riverside and is it easy to get around?
faq.a: The hotel is at 381 Charoen Rat Road in Wat Ket, on the east bank of the Ping River · It is about 10 minutes by car from the Night Bazaar, 15 minutes from the Old City and 15 minutes from Chiang Mai airport · The area is quiet and charming, with old temples and riverside cafés, but town is too far to walk (over 30 minutes), so rely on Grab or the hotel car.

faq.q: How much does At Pingnakorn Riverside cost and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. THB 1,400/night for the 42 sqm Deluxe Double in normal periods · There is also a Deluxe Twin, a Junior Suite (78 sqm) and a Family Suite (85 sqm) for families · Rooms here are known for being larger than the price · High-season rates (Nov–Feb) climb quickly, so compare several platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is At Pingnakorn Riverside best for?
faq.a: It is ideal for couples and families who want spacious rooms and a quiet riverside setting on a midrange budget · The colonial-meets-Lanna design and breakfast beside the Ping River are the standouts · If you want to walk straight into the tourist areas or are very sensitive to noise, a city-centre stay may suit you better.

faq.q: What is the noise like at At Pingnakorn Riverside and which room should I ask for?
faq.a: Reviews agree that soundproofing between rooms and from the corridor is weak, so you may hear your neighbours · If you are a light sleeper, ask for a room away from the corridor or on a quiet floor, and a recently renovated one, when booking or at check-in.

faq.q: Does At Pingnakorn Riverside have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes — an outdoor saltwater pool with a Jacuzzi and a children's pool in a leafy setting · A breakfast buffet is served beside the Ping River at the Nakara restaurant and is praised for its variety and good coffee · It can be slow or not kept hot at times, so go around the 7am opening for the freshest food and best seats.

faq.q: Are the rooms really spacious and what is the design like?
faq.a: Yes — standard rooms start at 42 sqm, larger than similarly priced hotels in Chiang Mai, with big bathrooms · The building is designed in an Eastern Colonial style blended with applied Lanna architecture from the reign of King Rama V, with timber tones and vintage furnishings · Last renovated in 2024, and reviews praise the distinctive, photogenic atmosphere throughout.
